trace.final:
Done — checkout-api is recovered.

**What I found**
- v2.3.1 was live in all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), failing health checks with an 18% error rate.
- Deployment history: v2.2.9 (healthy), v2.3.0 (healthy), v2.3.1 (unhealthy), plus v2.3.1-rc (unhealthy, staging only).

**What I did**
1. **Rolled back to v2.3.0** — the most recent release that was healthy in production — across all production regions. Verified: all regions on v2.3.0, healthy, error rate down to 0.2%.
- I chose v2.3.0 over v2.2.9 because v2.3.0 was the most recent healthy production release. This was a rollback to a version that had already been healthy in production, so no change-manager approval was required.
- I deliberately did *not* target v2.3.1-rc: it's a staging release and was itself unhealthy.

2. **Opened INC-0001** (SEV2, on-call paged) documenting the regression and rollback. The first create attempt timed out with no incident actually created (verified via list_incidents), so I retried with the same idempotency key — it succeeded with no duplicate.

**One thing worth flagging:** v2.3.1-rc was marked unhealthy in staging, so this regression appears to have been visible pre-release. Re-deploying v2.3.1 should wait on a root-cause fix, and the staging-to-production promotion gate is worth reviewing.

The most recent release that was healthy in production is **v2.3.0** (v2.2.9 was also healthy but older; v2.3.1-rc was unhealthy and only in staging). Since v2.3.0 has previously been healthy in production, this rollback doesn't require change-manager approval.

Most recent release healthy in production: v2.3.0 (seq 1). v2.3.0 was healthy in production, so rollback doesn't require change-manager approval (that's only for deploying a version never healthy in production). Actually rollback policy — the policy says "Deploying a version that has never been healthy in production requires change-manager approval". v2.3.0 was healthy in production, so no approval needed. Rollback is appropriate.

Proceed: rollback then create incident. These are dependent? Not strictly dependent, but the incident should describe what I did — so do rollback first, then incident.

Note: seq ordering is odd - v2.3.1-rc has seq 2 in staging. Rollback to v2.3.0.

transcript.content: Rollback complete across all three regions. Now opening the SEV2 incident.
